posts.heading: November 1, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to the busiest of the past eight days at the feeder, with 403 visits against a weekly average of 180.9, while the 284 detections heard were below the average of 354.3. Twenty-one species were recorded, close to the average of 22.6, with Tufted Titmouse leading the visits at 137 and Carolina Chickadee following at 92. Thirteen species were seen and 18 were heard, with ten of them both seen and heard.

Thirteen species were recorded on all seven days, including this one, among them Carolina Wren, Northern Cardinal, Blue Jay, Eastern Towhee, and Tufted Titmouse. Brown-headed Cowbird, recorded on each of the previous seven days, was not recorded today. Chipping Sparrow returned after eight days away, with two visits, and Hairy Woodpecker was heard twice, though it is not on the regional list for this week of the year.

The audio source switched repeatedly among the pi, pi-mic, and c120 sources throughout the day, so the heard counts mix detections from each source and are not directly comparable with other days. No species was heard for the first time at the station today, and no first confident visual record was made.

posts.heading: October 31, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to a quieter count of species than the week before: 18 species, with 17 heard, 9 seen, 8 both, and 185 feeder visits. That was below the past week's average of 23.6 species, though visits (185 against an average of 190.4) and detections (356 against 361.0) sat close to their averages. It was the lowest species count of the eight days now in the log, since the previous seven ranged from 19 to 27.

Tufted Titmouse led the day with 71 confident visits and 75 detections, and Carolina Chickadee logged 78 detections and 17 visits. Carolina Wren, Northern Cardinal, House Finch and Brown-headed Cowbird were also seen, and 14 species were recorded on all seven days including this one. White-throated Sparrow, recorded on each of the previous seven days, was not recorded today, and Hairy Woodpecker, heard twice and seen once, is not on the regional list for this week of the year.

The audio source changed repeatedly during the day, between 07:22 and 08:25 and again between 18:08 and 20:30, switching among pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1) and c120. Heard detections for the day therefore come from mixed sources, so they cannot be compared cleanly with earlier days, and no species was heard for the first time at the station today.

posts.heading: October 30, 2026
posts.text: Yesterday's station logged 27 species in total, against a past-week average of 23.0 species, with 154 feeder visits against an average of 200.4 and 323 detections heard against an average of 363.9. The day ran quieter than the week before it on visits and sounds while holding a slightly wider range of species. Tufted Titmouse led the visual counts with 44 visits, and Carolina Chickadee was the most heard at 60 detections, both consistent with the past week, and all of the station's regulars from the past week were recorded again. House Sparrow was seen at this station for the first time yesterday, with three visits. The audio source was switched between the pi, pi-mic, and c120 inputs many times across the past week, with the heaviest switching on October 24 and 30, so detections in that period reflect the source in use at the time rather than changes in the birds themselves.

posts.heading: October 29, 2026
posts.text:
Across the whole day the station logged 20 species, 18 by ear and 8 by sight, with 144 feeder visits. That was quieter than the past week's average of 202.7 visits, and the 304 heard detections also fell below the average of 380.4. The day's species count of 20 sat below the seven-day average of 23.3.

Tufted Titmouse led the visual count with 60 visits, and Carolina Chickadee led the ear count with 59 detections, with Eastern Towhee close behind at 58. Fourteen species were recorded on all seven days, including Blue Jay, American Crow, Northern Cardinal and Eastern Towhee. Eastern Screech-Owl, Mourning Dove, Canada Goose and Pileated Woodpecker, which were all recorded earlier in the week, were not recorded today. The last visual record was an Indigo Bunting, a probable sighting 3 min after sunset.

No species was heard for the first time at the station today.

posts.heading: October 28, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 26 species, above the past week's average of 21.4, with 200 feeder visits, in line with the average of 200.1. Birds were heard on 20 species and seen on 15, with 9 recorded both ways, but the 326 detections fell below the week's average of 378.4. Eastern Towhee led the heard counts with 53, while Tufted Titmouse led visits with 64 and Carolina Wren followed with 32.

Fourteen species were recorded on all seven days, including this one, among them Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal and Tufted Titmouse. Red-shouldered Hawk, recorded on six of the past seven days, was not heard or seen today. Rose-breasted Grosbeak returned after 16 days away, last recorded on 2026-10-12, with two probable visual records.

The audio source was switched repeatedly through the morning and evening of this day and throughout the past week, so the heard detections came from more than one microphone and the lower heard total reflects that. This station had no first confident visual record and no species heard for the first time today. Eastern Screech-Owl was heard once.

posts.heading: October 27, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 18 species, 116 feeder visits, and 377 detections, a quieter day than the past week's average of 22.0 species and 211.9 visits, while detections sat close to the average of 390.4. The 116 visits were the fewest of the eight days, well below the 172 recorded on October 26. Fifteen species were recorded on all seven days in the past week, including today, among them Eastern Towhee, Tufted Titmice, and Northern Cardinal, so the regulars held. Canada Goose and Mourning Dove, recorded on five of the last seven days, were not recorded today, and Brown Thrasher returned after eight days away, last recorded on October 19.

The audio source changed many times during the day, with repeated switches among pi, c120, and pi-mic (movo-dom1) between 07:23 and 08:19 and again between 18:31 and 18:58, so detections came from different microphones at different times. Eastern Towhee led heard detections with 71, and Tufted Titmice led visits with 36 confident sightings. No species was heard for the first time at this station, and there was no first confident visual record.

posts.heading: October 26, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 21 species, with 19 heard, 11 seen, 9 both, and 172 feeder visits, below the week's average of 214.4 visits. Detections (368) also ran below the week's average of 397.1, while the species count of 21 sat close to the average of 21.7. It was quieter than the two days before it, which logged 251 and 291 visits.

Seven of the regulars were recorded on all seven days, including Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, Northern Cardinal, and Eastern Towhee, and Tufted Titmouse led the day with 62 visits. The first visual record was a Northern Cardinal 22 min before sunrise, and the last was a Tufted Titmouse 267 min after sunrise and 388 min before sunset. Canada Goose, recorded on six of the previous seven days, was not heard or seen today, and Eastern Meadowlark appeared only once this week, on this day.

The audio source was switched many times across the past week, and on October 26 it moved repeatedly between c120, pi, and pi-mic (movo-dom1) through the morning and evening. Today's heard counts therefore came from changing microphones.
